## What it is

The peg the G2 holds in the real-world insertion test. It's the sim's peg (`rl_insert/peg_hole.py`, `add_peg`): Ø10 × 60 mm. The gripper holds 20 mm of it, centred on the pads, and 40 mm sticks out past the pad centre (TCP), which is about 20 mm past the G2's fingertips.

## Design notes

- Print it standing up, so the cross-section is a true circle. Grip the end that was on the bed: that end gets the slight flare a first layer leaves (elephant's foot), and the gripped end is the one that never goes into the hole.
- Measure the printed diameter with calipers. The clearance that matters is the real hole diameter minus the real peg diameter, not the modelled one.
- The sim gives the peg 20 g (`peg_mass`). A printed one is lighter (about 6 g in PLA at 100% infill), which doesn't matter: the grasp weld carries it.

## Don't

- Don't chamfer or round the ends. The sim's peg is a flat-ended cylinder, so a chamfered tip makes insertion easier in real life than in training and muddies the sim-to-real comparison. The lead-in lives on the hole, as in the sim.
- Don't print it lying down: the bottom flattens and the top sags, so it comes out oval.
